{"_meta":{"io.modelcontextprotocol/serverInfo":{"description":"Context7 provides up-to-date documentation and code examples for libraries and frameworks.","icons":[{"mimeType":"image/svg+xml","sizes":["any"],"src":"https://context7.com/context7-icon-green.svg"},{"mimeType":"image/png","sizes":["512x512"],"src":"https://context7.com/context7-icon-green.png"}],"name":"Context7","title":"Context7","version":"4.4.2","websiteUrl":"https://context7.com"}},"content":[{"text":"### Import test module in ES modules\n\nSource: https://github.com/nodejs/node/blob/v25.9.0/doc/api/test.md\n\nImport the test module using the node: scheme in ES module syntax.\n\n```mjs\nimport test from 'node:test';\n```\n\n--------------------------------\n\n### Import JSON modules with import attributes\n\nSource: https://github.com/nodejs/node/blob/v25.9.0/doc/api/esm.md\n\nUse the 'with { type: 'json' }' attribute to import JSON files as modules. Required for both static import and dynamic import() syntax.\n\n```javascript\nimport fooData from './foo.json' with { type: 'json' };\n```\n\n```javascript\nconst { default: barData } =\n  await import('./bar.json', { with: { type: 'json' } });\n```\n\n### import() expressions\n\nSource: https://github.com/nodejs/node/blob/v25.9.0/doc/api/esm.md\n\nDynamic `import()` provides an asynchronous way to import modules. It is supported in both CommonJS and ES modules and can load both types of modules.\n\n--------------------------------\n\n### Conditional exports > Node.js Conditions > import\n\nSource: https://github.com/nodejs/node/blob/v25.9.0/doc/api/packages.md\n\nThe `\"import\"` condition matches when the package is loaded via `import` or `import()`, or via any top-level import or resolve operation by the ECMAScript module loader. It is always mutually exclusive with `\"require\"`.\n\n--------------------------------\n\n### importModuleDynamically > Function Behavior\n\nSource: https://github.com/nodejs/node/blob/v25.9.0/doc/api/vm.md\n\nWhen importModuleDynamically is a function, it is invoked when import() is called in compiled code, allowing customization of how the requested module should be compiled and evaluated. The Node.js instance must be launched with the --experimental-vm-modules flag for this option to work. If the flag is not set, the callback will be ignored and any actual calls to import() will reject with an error.","type":"text"}],"isError":false}
